opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

amount.raw: Scheme A up to £200; Scheme B up to £500 (up to £750 for Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored); Scheme C up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics Society 'junior scientist' members. Scheme A open to undergraduate, Master's and PhD student members and postdoctoral members within six years of PhD viva. Schemes B & C open to PhD student and postdoctoral members within six years of PhD viva. Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at conferences on research in Genetics. Three streams: (A) Genetics Society/SIG meetings, (B) non-Genetics Society meetings, (C) virtual conferences. Bi-monthly deadlines on 1st of Feb, Apr, Jun, Aug, Oct, Dec.

opportunities.title: Training Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society studying or working in the UK, or attending a course held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be a member for at least one year. Supervisor must be a member for student applicants.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques. Quarterly deadlines at midnight on 15th February, May, August and November.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be a member for at least one year. Supervisor must be a member for student applicants.
opportunities.summary: Awards to cover travel and accommodation costs associated with a field-based genetic research project, funded by income from the Society's journal Heredity. Research should produce results suitable for publication in Heredity. Quarterly deadlines on 1st February, May, August and November.

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any member of the Genetics Society with caring responsibilities, regardless of age of the person they care for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need.
opportunities.summary: Award of up to £60/day to support attendance at a Society meeting for members with caring responsibilities. Competitive, applied for prior to the meeting, claimable in arrears on production of receipts.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting Sponsorship

amount.raw: A specific lecture for a few hundred pounds; a session up to about £1,000; major sponsorship of an entire meeting several thousand pounds (major sponsorship levels for the last 12 months between £1,000 and £2,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics Society members. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society. Members may apply at any time of the year, at least three months in advance of the event. Applications reviewed at the end of each month.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant
opportunities.summary: Grants to support public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually. Funding covers eligible travel and materials costs (UK-based, budget/economy class). Two deadlines per year (1st March and 1st October).

opportunities.title: Special Interest Group (SIG) Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics Society members / genetics research communities. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of research meetings on particular themes for genetics research communities wishing to run regular series of meetings. Applications to become a new Special Interest Group should be submitted at least three months before the first meeting.
